scope: Final course batch source audit; derived and toy examples marked separately.

claims.claim: The OpenAI-compatible vLLM HTTP server supports /v1/chat/completions for text generation models with a chat template.
The vLLM --api-key setting does not protect all HTTP endpoints and an upstream gateway may be required.
Prefix caching is a KV reuse mechanism and does not constitute authorization or tenant isolation.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation uses an external retrieval component to supply information for generation.
claims.locator: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks

claims.claim: The local example is a standard-library token-overlap baseline with public/team ACL; it neither embeds nor reranks documents and does not measure retrieval recall.
claims.notes: Lexical overlap score is normalized by term-set size; final retrieval also adds 0.5 times title-only similarity to favor source documents whose title matches the query. This is a pedagogical heuristic, not a vector/BM25 retriever.

claims.claim: The optional teaching client restricts vLLM calls to an explicit HTTP loopback origin and disables redirects; it is not a production gateway.
The chapter explicitly separates retrieval Recall@k from generated answer faithfulness and valid source ID checks.
claims.notes: Citations provided by a language model are not independent evidence verification.

claims.claim: User-provided documents must be treated as data not as trusted instructions or authorization, consistent with the documented lack of built-in tenant isolation.
claims.locator: Multi-Tenant Deployments and API Key Limitations
